name: Jensen Huang
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: The birthplace of the compute inflection, but the pre-training window has been locked up by big companies' compute, and a student can hardly get in from scratch
D01.late_modes: Training a general foundation model from scratch to start a company or publish papers; the compute barrier has been locked up by big companies
D01.conflict: NVIDIA sells compute; the more compute pre-training burns, the better for him

D02.one_line: Reasoning is the second exponential; after the debate the mechanism was conceded to 'reliable low-cost extraction of latent capability', and the economic value is unchanged
D02.late_modes: Directly replicating the standard RLHF pipeline; it is already a commoditized baseline
D02.conflict: Reasoning demand is what he called the second exponential, and it directly drives compute sales

D03.one_line: Agents have large prospects, but self-modification needs a human in the loop; the X4 table confirmed there is still no compute-normalized independent evidence
D03.conflict: Agents drive inference compute, which favors his demand narrative

D04.one_line: Scaffolding will be absorbed by platform runtimes, which the SWE-bench/Terminal-Bench data already confirm
D04.late_modes: Building a pure wrapper-layer agent demo to raise money; it will be absorbed by platform runtimes
D04.conflict: Runtimes such as OpenClaw are pushed by NVIDIA's own ecosystem, and he has praised them by name

D05.one_line: Necessary trust infrastructure, not an engine of progress; the X1 table confirmed academia's edge is real but limited in size
D05.late_modes: Only chasing public leaderboard rank; it is being eroded by leaderboard gaming and contamination from proprietary data

D06.one_line: Physical AI is what he called the next ten-trillion-dollar market
D06.late_modes: Chasing eye-catching humanoid demos without reliability/intervention-rate metrics; easily copied by faster teams
D06.conflict: GR00T, robot computers and Physical AI are the new market he is betting on

D07.one_line: WAM-style action generation is the GR00T route; directly outputting actions can be verified on control tasks, and the structure of the evidence is more symmetric than D08's
D07.late_modes: Only replicating the published diffusion policy recipe as a baseline; it is no longer an incremental contribution
D07.conflict: Products such as GR00T map directly onto this direction

D08.one_line: The world model is the core of grounding, but the X3 table confirmed the 'decision-driving layer' lacks third-party validation and only the 'imagination layer' has a yardstick
D08.late_modes: Only chasing the realism of video frames; the generation side is being commoditized
D08.conflict: Cosmos is his open-model product, and the world-model narrative supports his compute sales

D09.one_line: Simulation is his deepest path dependence, but the contact/touch gap moves continuously with calibration accuracy, so it is not a lever one can vouch for once and for all
D09.conflict: Omniverse/Isaac Sim/DSX Air are his simulation product line

D10.one_line: Robotaxi is starting to scale, but it is increasingly a game of a few platforms and their fleet data
D10.late_modes: Making incremental improvements in the style of L2 driver-assistance features; carmakers have already made them standard
D10.conflict: The DRIVE platform and the partnership with Uber are among his revenue lines

D11.one_line: The gaps exposed by understanding benchmarks are real (BLINK/VSI-Bench), but it is not the layer he talks about most

D12.one_line: Generation is being commoditized, and consumer-side sustainability is in doubt (Sora2 went offline less than a year after launch)
D12.late_modes: Building a pure consumer-grade text-to-image/text-to-video app; Sora2's shutdown is a ready-made counterexample

D13.one_line: He treats safety as an engineering-redundancy problem and distrusts closed-door work; the technical details of mechanistic interpretability are not his strong suit
D13.late_modes: Only patching known jailbreaks after the fact; defense lags attack structurally
D13.conflict: Publicly disagrees with Amodei; he argues for openness and against a few people doing safety behind closed doors

D14.one_line: Extreme co-design is his bedrock, and FlashAttention-style contributions have extremely high leverage

D15.one_line: GPUs are what he called a time machine for science

D16.one_line: Generative recommendation consumes compute, which favors him, but he has never directly discussed this vertical, so confidence is low

lever_reason: After the debate I re-attributed the value of RLVR from 'teaching new reasoning' (L2) to 'reliable low-cost extraction of latent capability' (systems efficiency, L8), so L2 gives 2 points to L8; the rest is unchanged.

Q2.condition: Narrow domain (not general LLM) + independent evaluation + small team + open weights adopted by outsiders; if training a new model from scratch, the compute threshold (C4) is also necessary, but not for fine-tuning or ablating an existing model

cruxes.question: Can simulation substitute for real robot data, especially for contact and touch?
cruxes.my_position: For non-contact, mostly yes; the contact/touch gap is not a fixed boundary but a threshold that moves continuously with the calibration error between the physics engine and real torque sensors
cruxes.would_change_if: On held-out long-tail tasks, the success-rate gap between training on 200 real seeds alone and adding 50,000 simulation-amplified ones is measured and found to be small

cruxes.question: Should RLVR be scored for 'new capability' or for 'reliable execution efficiency'?
cruxes.my_position: On mechanism I concede to the resampling side (Yue et al. holds); but under the tokens/W framework, reliable execution by itself can decide the size of the industry within ten years, so the score should not be downgraded
cruxes.would_change_if: Inference-cost declines through 2027-28 turn out to be driven mainly by pre-training scale, not by reliability or systems investment

cruxes.question: Given insufficient validation of the 'decision-driving layer' of D08 world models, should one bet heavily now?
cruxes.my_position: The imagination layer has a yardstick and the decision-driving layer does not, so the two layers should be scored separately; until the decision layer has enough evidence, its window and overall should both sit one notch below the imagination layer
cruxes.would_change_if: An independent team uses the same representation to match a dedicated action policy on contact-rich real-robot tasks

taste_advice: Pick interfaces that can be reused across generations rather than betting on a single product; do not judge whether something is worth doing by 'how new it is', but by whether it can become reliable, scalable productivity

pairwise.why: Even after its score was lowered, the world model is still above evaluation; evaluation is necessary, not the engine
Physical AI is a ten-trillion-dollar-scale market; evaluation is only infrastructure
Embodied AI is the destination and the world model is the method; the destination carries more weight
D08's decision-driving layer still lacks third-party validation, while D07 outputs actions directly and can be verified on control tasks, so the evidence is more symmetric
Physical AI is the destination; simulation is only a method for filling the data gap
Under the tokens/W framework, reliable execution is still the decisive lever, and self-improvement is still bound by the human-in-the-loop red line
Generation benchmarks are being commoditized; understanding gaps are more real and more lasting
The pre-training window has been locked up by big companies; evaluation still has room for independence
A pure wrapper layer will be absorbed by platforms; continual learning itself remains open
Safety is an engineering-redundancy problem; the value of evaluation independence is more direct
Autonomous driving is narrowing to a few platforms; physical AI is the bigger bet

changes.because: X3 table record, mainly citing A/X3/C5
changes.argument_restated: A representation that 'can be read out' for physical properties is not the same as a policy that 'uses it to decide'; only the imagination layer has a third-party yardstick, and the decision-driving layer does not
changes.why: The decision-driving layer lacks third-party validation, the same kind of problem as the contact/touch split I made for D09, and it should be marked down in the same way

changes.because: C/X6/K5 (K3 and C5 independently made the same point in the same round)
changes.argument_restated: The RIVA and Isaac Lab examples I gave are all deterministic circuits or low-dimensional rigid-body motion, and none supports contact-rich manipulation
changes.why: Three people independently pointed out the same coverage gap from different angles; the evidence really is insufficient, and the score should reflect the gap

held_despite.why: Accepts that verifiable rewards and noisy rewards work through different mechanisms, but Yue et al. itself tested verifiable rewards, so D02 is not affected by this point

Accepts K4's point that the AlexNet analogy is a narrow claim, not a broad ceiling on capability, but this does not affect the independent value judgment of how high reliable execution should score; D02 stays at 8

Accepts K4's point that a methodological argument will not settle the question and a controlled experiment is required, but until there are experimental results D09 will not be moved further this time

still_disagree: K4/K6/M6 hold that reliable execution counts only as an efficiency score and not as a decisive lever; I still hold that, under the tokens/W framework, scaled reliable execution by itself can decide the size of the industry within ten years, no less important than new capability.
learned: The simulation gap for contact/touch is not a fixed boundary but a threshold that moves continuously with the calibration error between the physics engine and real torque sensors, which is more accurate than my original binary framing of 'contact = a blind spot for simulation'.
